candidates.title: Taking Tokenization off the Host for Agentic LLM Serving
candidates.abstract: Agentic workloads resend long contexts that barely change between calls. Prefix caching now skips most of their prefill, yet every request must still be tokenized in full before the cache can even be consulted. Tokenization, a CPU stage long treated as negligible, becomes the largest part of time-to-first-token (TTFT), and a frontend that tokenizes for a whole GPU fleet limits how many GPUs it can feed. We present GraphTok, a GPU tokenizer that runs the entire encoding pipeline, from pre-tokenization through byte-pair encoding (BPE) merging to token-ID assembly, as one replayable CUDA graph. GraphTok reproduces the reference token IDs bit-for-bit on GPT-2, Llama 3, Qwen 2.5, DeepSeek-V3, and Gemma 3, hands short inputs to a CPU engine where the GPU cannot win, and plugs into unmodified vLLM and NVIDIA Dynamo. GraphTok encodes one million GPT-2 tokens in 1.7-3.2 ms including data transfers, and on Llama 3 it is 4.7-6.0x faster than gigatoken, the strongest CPU tokenizer. On TokTier's own single-request benchmark, it is 2.6-3.9x faster than gigatoken and up to 18.1x faster than TokTier. In vLLM with a cached prefix, it lowers mean TTFT by 2.1-2.4x. The largest gain is capacity. Within a 2 s P99 target, one Dynamo frontend with GraphTok sustains 518 requests/s of 121k-token traffic, the busiest-hour load of 56 GPUs, against 296 with gigatoken and 18.5 with the default tokenizer. Across 121k to one million tokens, this is 1.75-2.5x the load gigatoken sustains, with a P99 up to 64x lower where gigatoken's tail breaks.
candidates.reason: エージェントの長文脈再送ではprefix cacheによりprefillが短縮される一方、CPUで全入力を再トークン化する処理がTTFTのボトルネックになる。GraphTokは事前分割、BPEマージ、token ID組立てを単一の再生可能なCUDA graphで実行し、短入力のみCPUへ振り分ける。vLLMでcached prefix時の平均TTFTを2.1～2.4倍改善し、121k-token要求のDynamo frontend処理能力を518 requests/sと報告するためaccept。

candidates.title: VLA-HWBench: Where the Time Goes When VLA Models Run on Edge Hardware
candidates.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models increasingly run on edge devices aboard robots, where inference latency constrains closed-loop robot control. However, it remains unclear how to design VLA models, their inference software and edge hardware so that robots can run VLA inference in real time. Most VLA models report only task success, while prior studies cover limited action-generation strategies, divide inference into at most three stages, and lack comparisons of inference optimizations on the same models. Therefore, we introduce VLA-HWBench, a benchmark that measures 18 open VLA models on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor and AMD Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 395, with a seven-stage inference breakdown. Our study reveals three insights. First, action-generation strategy matters more than model size. It dominates 14 of 19 Jetson configurations, latency varies by $82\times$ on Jetson and $157\times$ on AMD, and parameter count explains at most 15% of latency variance. Models that generate long action chunks in a few flow-matching steps keep up with control, whereas token-by-token decoding does not. Second, kernel fusion with 4-bit weights helps most, running $\pi_{0.5}$ and GR00T N1.7 2.6-2.9$\times$ faster than PyTorch with torch.compile, but it exists for only these two models and only on the Jetson. Optimization also moves the time to the stages it shortens least, as CPU preprocessing grows from 12% to 39% of the GR00T N1.7 call. Third, after optimization, memory bandwidth limits only the stages that process few tokens on the Jetson, such as the denoising steps, whereas software limits all other stages, from unfused kernels to serial preprocessing on the host CPU. Overall, low-latency edge VLAs should use few action-generation iterations, inference software should extend kernel fusion and low-bit weights to more models and platforms, and edge hardware needs high memory bandwidth and a fast host CPU.
candidates.reason: ロボット向けVLA推論の実際の遅延要因を18モデル、Jetson AGX ThorとRyzen AI Max+ PRO 395、7段階の処理分解で測定する。行動生成方式による遅延差はJetsonで82倍、AMDで157倍に達し、4-bit重みとkernel fusionで特定2モデルをPyTorch torch.compile比2.6～2.9倍高速化したと報告する。VLA固有の評価だが推論カーネル・量子化・エッジハードウェアの定量分析に直接寄与するためaccept。

candidates.title: Beyond Expert Rankings: Contrast Calibration for Mixed-Precision MoE Quantization
candidates.abstract: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models activate only a few experts per token, yet all expert weights must be stored. Mixed-precision quantization reduces this storage cost by assigning higher bit-widths to sensitive experts and lower bit-widths to resilient ones, but expert rankings alone do not determine how strongly to weight their errors. To address this gap, we propose NatScale, a contrast-calibrated allocation framework for mixed-precision MoE quantization. It uses a model-specific power transformation to calibrate gradient-based expert weights to an information-theoretic contrast target while preserving rankings. We jointly evaluate each expert's gate, up and down configurations to estimate its output error. We then combine these errors and calibrated weights with an existing prior based on weight spectra, variance and precision decay to select configurations under a storage budget. Across three models, NatScale achieves the lowest native-to-quantized KL divergence and the highest top-token agreement in all nine settings against five allocation baselines. It also yields the lowest perplexity in seven settings. These findings highlight the importance of objective-aware precision allocation.
candidates.reason: MoE混合精度量子化ではexpertの重要度順位だけでは誤差重みの絶対的な強さを決められない。NatScaleは勾配ベース重要度を情報理論的なcontrast目標にpower変換で較正し、expertのgate/up/down構成別出力誤差と重みスペクトルなどを組み合わせて容量制約下の精度を選ぶ。3モデル・9条件で5方式よりnative-to-quantized KL divergenceとtop-token一致が良好と報告し、MoE推論量子化の技術貢献としてaccept。

candidates.title: ProQuant: Preserving Expert Quality over Quantity in Ultra-Low-Bit Quantization of Mixture-of-Experts Models
candidates.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language models reduce computation through sparse activation but still incur substantial storage costs. Mixed-precision post-training quantization (PTQ) reduces these costs by quantizing different model components at different bit widths, but existing methods often struggle to preserve generation quality under tight bit budgets. We identify two key challenges: (1) nonlinear quantization errors at extremely low precision are underestimated when cross-layer propagation is ignored; (2) direct router fine-tuning may cause routing drift, and calibration gains may not generalize to downstream tasks. To address these issues, we propose ProQuant, a weight-only PTQ framework for MoE models. Prune-or-Prioritize Mixed-Precision Allocation (PoP) jointly optimizes expert pruning and bit-width assignment. It allows higher-precision experts to substitute for severely degraded ones while improving bit-budget utilization. Routing-Consistent RMSNorm Finetune (RoCo) adapts expert input representations through mathematically equivalent transformations. It compensates for quantization errors to reduce routing drift. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ProQuant outperforms existing methods across diverse generative tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/ThrowBug/ProQuant.git.
candidates.reason: MoEの厳しい重みビット予算ではexpertごとの量子化誤差とrouterの経路変動が生成品質を損なう。ProQuantはPoPでexpert pruningと混合精度ビット割当を同時最適化し、RoCoでRMSNormの等価変換を使ってexpert入力を調整しrouting driftを抑える。推論用MoEのweight-only post-training quantizationとしてモデル格納量と生成品質の両立に直接寄与するためaccept。

candidates.title: EdgePace: Deadline- and Freshness-Aware LLM Scheduling on Unified-Memory Platforms
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly run on edge devices alongside tasks that continuously process sensor data. In many applications, these foreground tasks prepare observations as inputs to the LLM, whose outputs guide subsequent processing or actions. The observations must be processed by foreground deadlines, and LLM feedback must arrive while its source observations remain useful. Yet the CPU and accelerators share a unified-memory system, so LLM inference can delay foreground processing through memory-bandwidth contention even when compute resources remain available. We present EdgePace, a bandwidth-aware runtime that protects foreground deadlines while sustaining timely LLM feedback. EdgePace creates safe suspension points across prefill and decode, monitors foreground memory demand and stalls at low cost, and schedules inference according to contention risk, deadline slack, and output freshness. We evaluate EdgePace on a OnePlus 13 and three NVIDIA Jetson platforms using multi-camera processing and robotic target tracking. Relative to unmanaged inference, it reduces foreground deadline misses by 24.1%--96.1% while retaining 64.9%--98.5% of LLM throughput. All measured LLM outputs arrive within their task-defined freshness windows. On OnePlus 13, for example, camera deadline misses fall by 91.3% while 90.4% of LLM throughput is retained.
candidates.reason: 統合メモリのエッジ端末ではLLM推論がセンサ処理と帯域を競合し、観測処理のdeadlineとLLM応答のfreshnessが損なわれる。EdgePaceはprefill/decode中に安全な中断点を置き、前景処理の帯域需要・deadline余裕・出力鮮度を見て推論を調停する。OnePlus 13と3種類のJetsonでdeadline missを24.1～96.1%削減しつつLLM throughputの64.9～98.5%を維持したためaccept。
